description: Journey through the cryptic corridors of code. Unravel the secrets encoded in the shadows. Welcome to the realm where algorithms whisper in binary tongues. Dare to explore, for within lies the essence of innovation.

paragraphs: I'm Felipe, a Computer Science Engineer (Ingº en Informática) from Santiago, Chile, with extensive experience in Systems Architecture, Distributed Systems, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Complex Systems Engineering, Software Engineering, Cybersecurity, Strategic Cyber Intelligence, OSINT, Cyber Counterterrorism, Open Source Software (OSS) Engineering, and Research & Development (R&D). My work focuses on designing secure, resilient, scalable, and high-performance systems by combining systems architecture, distributed systems engineering, site reliability engineering, complex systems…

I still keep my late-90s/early-2000s-era Perl book — The “Camel Book” (1,000+ pages my well-worn copy) — a reminder of long nights with coffee, dim light, and room-heating computers with painfully bad CRT screens, when computers were heavy tower cases — not millimeters-thin devices. That was my era: experimenting with Ethernet network cables in my bedroom, running multiple rigs, giving old hardware a second life with Mandrake Linux. Later, I carried that obsession into engineering school.

Some of my earliest engineering memories are IRC nights, SSH sessions, and multi-user Linux systems — learning by building, breaking, and fixing. Forged through Linux the hard way: compiling kernels, hacking connectivity, and learning through friction — not convenience.
